::: {#exr-geometric}
## The geometric series

::: {.lm-solution}
1. Multiplying the sum $s_n$ by $1 - q$, all terms but the first and the last cancel: $(1 - q) s_n = 1 - q^{n+1}$.

1. For $|q| < 1$, $q^{n+1} \to 0$, so $\sum_{k=0}^{\infty} q^k = 1 / (1 - q)$. With $q = 1/10$:
   $$
     \sum_{k=1}^{\infty} 9 \cdot 10^{-k} = \frac{9}{10} \cdot \frac{1}{1 - 1/10} = 1.
   $$
:::
:::

```{julia}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
include("src/partial_sums.jl")
```

::: {#exr-alternating}
## The alternating harmonic series

### Implementation

::: {.lm-solution}
The function is in `src/partial_sums.jl` (see the appendix).
:::

### Errors

::: {.lm-solution}
```{julia}
sums = partial_sums(1000)
ns = [10, 100, 1000]
[ns abs.(sums[ns] .- log(2))]
```

The error is about $1 / (2n)$: one more correct digit needs ten times as many terms. The geometric series with $q = 1/10$ gains one digit with each term.
:::
:::

## Appendix

### `src/partial_sums.jl`

```{.julia .number-lines}
# The partial sums s_1, ..., s_n of the alternating harmonic series.
function partial_sums(n)
    s = 0.0
    sums = Float64[]
    for k in 1:n
        s += (-1)^(k + 1) / k
        push!(sums, s)
    end
    return sums
end
```
